scope: Linux x64 console buffering, inherited-child ordering, full-pipe backpressure, and worker diagnostics/lifetime. Supplementary ordinary-Lean controls and 21 unchanged upstream registrations; not a complete suite or cross-platform result.
findings: Default console writes used Node streams and bypassed native FILE buffering. stderr is unbuffered; stdout retains normal libc buffering and explicit/normal-exit flushes.

Native Lean flushes std::cout before spawn only when the child inherits stdin. The initial inherited-stdin control passed before repair; a refined null-stdin control exposed the difference in every engine.

Node default Worker forwarding and the ordinary Readable.pipe end branch each implicitly access process.stdout/stderr, changing shared pipe descriptors to O_NONBLOCK. Descriptor-backed forwarding with explicit end handling preserves flags.

Worker diagnostic reads must not independently keep an unreferenced worker alive. The Node adapter checks private kIncrementsPortRef/kStartedReading symbols before matching the default lifetime behavior.

The first supplementary backpressure fixture closed a descriptor while a delayed reader could still run after flush failure; this fixture cleanup defect caused one diagnostic SIGSEGV. The corrected fixture cancels a pending timer or waits for an active reader after closing the write side. All original failures are retained; no upstream test changed.
remainingGaps: Private Node worker stream layout is validated only on Node 24.13.1 here; other versions need validation.
Terminal behavior, pre-existing nonblocking standard descriptors, forced exit, regular-file process-exit flushing and native non-Linux behavior remain open.
Bun full-compiler results use the disclosed Linux stack helper, not a stock cross-platform configuration.
Full upstream suites and the complete packaged runtime remain unfinished; no remaining difference is established fundamental.
